label: prop:rational_algebra_limit
title: Rational algebra and bounded displacement

proof: Normalize the three data points, verify the cross-multiplied equations algebraically, then use the existing secant interiority theorem and d = min(s-a,b-s). Projection gives the 0.3d margins.

label: prop:rational_closed_update
title: Closed proposals and guarded closing
hypotheses: Sign-changing bracket; candidate in the closed interval; nonzero true evaluation; sign update. Positive supplied tolerance for closing.
proof: A collapsed retained interval would contradict the strict sign product. SourceProposal implies closed membership; guarded closing preserves it. The operational assembly derives candidate membership from these facts.

label: thm:rational_capped
title: Inheritance of the capped width theorem
status: Proved by reuse of the original phase/schedule proof
hypotheses: Continuous f on initial sign bracket; closed proposals and true updates; original capped Step B M with initial bisection and B >= 1/2.
proof: Reuse the existing width Run, global width bound, finite tolerance theorem and nested-interval theorem. Endpoint reuse consumes a step; it does not reset the clock. B=2, M=3 yields Wn <= W0 / 2^floor(n/7), an amortized bound from initialization.

label: thm:rational_uncapped_alternative
title: Uncapped width–residual alternative
status: Proved from transitions; not a model assumption
hypotheses: Nonnegative widths/residuals; nonincreasing widths; real bisections; advancing phase clock; continuation only through width success or residual decrease; minimum <= previous residual; 0 <= eta < 1. No continuity needed.
proof: If widths are arbitrarily small, monotonicity implies their convergence to zero. Otherwise their positive lower bound forces finitely many bisections. The threshold in the last phase tends to zero, so eventually every step satisfies R(n+1) < eta R(n).

label: thm:rational_uncapped_roots
title: Residual, zero-set and unique-root convergence
status: Proved for the continuous sign-bracketed model
hypotheses: Theorem 4 (legacy alias R4) plus continuity on the compact initial interval and true sign updates. Uniqueness is needed only for convergence to one specified root.
proof: In the width branch reuse the old nested-interval theorem and continuity. In the residual branch no further estimate is needed. A compact-subsequence contradiction proves eventual proximity to a true zero. Uniqueness turns that proximity into point convergence.

label: prop:rational_closing_termination
title: Width stopping from the actual closing operation
status: Proved with dynamic tolerances; spacing is derived
hypotheses: Operational SourceRun; unique zero on the initial interval; 0 <= eta < 1; tolerance(n) >= tau0 > 0. Exact real arithmetic, no claimed 200-visit bound.
proof: SourceRun.exactRun derives membership and schedule from the step equations. Infinitely many bisections force a width stop. Otherwise the interpolation tail converges to the unique root, while failure of the width test makes closing enforce steps of length at least tau0/2. This contradicts point convergence.

Normalized rawPoint error tends to K; denominator guards are proved eventually. Analytic specializations are retained but not required.

label: lem:local_tribonacci_order

hypotheses: Nonzero error sequence tending to zero; eventually e(n+3)=C(n)e(n+2)e(n+1)e(n); C(n) tends to nonzero K. The convergence premise is independently discharged for three small seeds and bounded coefficients in LocalAssembly.
proof: Prove the unique cubic root and rational enclosure 1.839<tau<1.840. Take logarithms; a positive quadratic energy bounds the stable forced recurrence. A proved geometric-tail contraction yields a zero log defect; exponentiation gives the exact Q-order constant.

label: thm:local_alternating
title: Safeguard-preserving alternating local regime
status: Fully proved: C3 hypotheses and the initial state imply the actual guarded trajectory and tribonacci Q-order
hypotheses: Local C3, simple root, nonzero second derivative and K>0. The theorem chooses one radius. Initial State has a sign bracket, both strictly exterior discarded-side histories in that radius and fresh true working ordinates. Exact real arithmetic, zero tolerances and no iteration budget. No future invariant, error recurrence, coefficient bound or limit is assumed.
proof: The uniform coefficient lemma is derived by sequential contradiction. Differentiability supplies secant and residual estimates; C2 and nonzero curvature decide the actual true-ordinate selector. A common radius satisfies clamp and residual42 inequalities. The true-sign/AB transition preserves both history records and fresh ordinates, proves no fallback and geometric convergence. Two crossings derive the latest-three recurrence. The C3 coefficient limit then gives genuine Q-order with its exact constant.

label: prop:local_pair_cycle
title: Invariant two-step cone and cubic pair recurrence
status: Fully proved: C3 interpolation yields a uniform invariant two-step regime of the actual guarded state iteration
hypotheses: Local C3, simple root, nonzero second derivative and K<0. The theorem chooses theta and radius. Initial fresh state has both local exterior histories and the signed separated cone. Exact real arithmetic, zero tolerances and no iteration budget. Uniform coefficients, their limits, future guards, invariance and error convergence are conclusions.
proof: The exact mixed-data formula gives a normalized second coefficient without a cancelling relative remainder. A shrinking-cone sequential argument derives both coefficients bounded strictly between 2K and K/2 and all denominator guards. Scaled secant and actual AB bounds make both candidates pass clamp, closing and residual42 tests. Both source orientations are proved, including rawPoint endpoint symmetry. Actual two-update transitions restore fresh ordinates and the next cone. Induction transports the concrete pair orbit to the actual state orbit and derives separation and coefficient limits.

label: cor:local_cycle_orders
title: Alternating exponents 9/5 and 5/3 with exact constants

Exact logarithmic/real-power identities give Q-order3 for both subsequences and the 9/5,5/3 successive quotient limits with their constants. The geometric mean is sqrt3; no single consecutive-step Q-order sqrt3 is claimed.

label: prop:local_one_sided
title: Nondegenerate one-sided golden-ratio order
status: Fully proved from the stated convergent one-sided tail and actual AB updates; bounded scaling is derived
hypotheses: Local C3 simple root; fixed opposite endpoint in the chosen small neighbourhood; nonzero convergent same-side unmodified rational tail with valid interpolation data; initial working factor in (0,1], and subsequent weights given by the actual abFactor. A nonzero limiting coefficient gives the order. No uniform scaling bound, subsequent weight monotonicity, or rate is assumed. Automatic global entry and C=0 remain outside the statement.
proof: The exact no-cross identity bounds delta by a cap whose limit is proved from fixed-node divided differences. Actual AB updates imply positivity and monotonicity of the weights. A tail bound extends to the full sequence; hence the weight has a positive limit. The connected C3 theorem then derives the two-error coefficient limit and golden Q-order, for either sign of the derivative.
